title: mesh_route_dispatch plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `mesh_route_dispatch` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component MeshRouteDispatchConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

MeshRouteBackendTlsConfig.description:
Strict route-local backend TLS override for mesh_route_dispatch.
Unknown keys (for example `client_certpath` or
`verify_server_certificate`) fail admission instead of silently
disabling intended mTLS materials or verification.

`client_cert_path` and `client_key_path` must be supplied together.
A `system://` `server_ca_cert_path` cannot be combined with
`verify_server_cert: false` (the same contradiction Proxy and Upstream
admission reject); that pairing is a runtime check because the schema
cannot condition on a value prefix and a sibling boolean at once.

Admin writes of a `mesh_route_dispatch` plugin config apply the
Proxy/Upstream backend TLS reference admission to `client_cert_path`,
`client_key_path`, and `server_ca_cert_path` in every
`rules[].destination.backend_tls`: when admin namespace-claim
enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with
enforcement off, an `operator` may set only inline PEM, `system://`,
or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace, and any other
reference it introduces is refused with `400` before the material is
loaded. A value already stored at the same rule index and field is
exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted.

MeshRouteBackoffStrategy.description:
Strict route-local retry delay strategy for mesh_route_dispatch. Each
delay is bounded to `[0, 300000]` ms by the shared gateway
`RetryConfig` field validation the route policy runs; `base_ms` must
additionally not exceed `max_ms`, which JSON Schema cannot express
across two sibling properties and is therefore a runtime-only check.

MeshRouteDispatchConfig.description:
Plugin: mesh_route_dispatch — Per-request route override driven by
method / header / query-param predicates. Closes the Istio
`VirtualService.http[].match` header/method gap without extending
the `Proxy` schema. Runs after authentication, authorization, and
rate limiting — admission decisions still use the public listener
identity; only downstream `before_proxy` plugins and backend
dispatch see the effective override destination.

At least one rule is required unless `weighted_splits` is set. When multiple plugin instances run on
one proxy, each matching instance replaces the override destination
set by earlier instances. Per-rule `backend_tls` is direct-backend
only (`upstream_id` destinations inherit TLS from the referenced
Upstream).

Unknown keys are rejected at every owned nesting level, including
route-local `retry` / backoff and destination `backend_tls`
(`additionalProperties: false` / serde `deny_unknown_fields`). Shared
gateway `RetryConfig` and `BackendTlsConfig` schemas remain open for
other consumers; mesh routes use `MeshRouteRetryConfig` and
`MeshRouteBackendTlsConfig`.

`rules` may be empty only when `weighted_splits` lists at least one
split (an instance that only resolves weighted splits).

items.description:
One ordered route rule. `destination` is required — and must
carry at least one override field — unless the rule carries a
`redirect` (which answers the request itself and needs no
backend). First match wins.

name.description:
Optional operator label for the rule: 1-128 printable ASCII
characters without whitespace. A match publishes
`mesh_route_dispatch.rule_index` (the rule's zero-based
position) and, when set, `mesh_route_dispatch.rule_name`
transaction-log metadata; both are withdrawn when a
NodeWaypoint authorization veto refuses the matched
destination.

match.description:
Match criteria — all configured fields must match for the
rule to fire. At least one of `methods`/`headers`/
`without_headers`/`query_params`/`authority`/
`source_namespace`/`uri`/`port` must be
configured, UNLESS the rule carries a route action
(`request_transform`, `response_transform`, `fault`,
`rewrite`, `redirect`, `timeout_ms`,
`timeout_disabled: true`, `request_timeout_ms`,
`attempt_timeout_ms`, `retry`, or
`retry_disabled: true`), which makes an empty match the
translator's deliberate action-only catch-all. An empty
match with no route action is rejected at load time because
it would silently shadow every later rule. `ignore_uri_case`
is not a predicate: it decorates `uri` and is rejected
without one.

oneOf.description:
Bare-string back-compat form, interpreted as Exact.
Must be a non-empty RFC 9110 method token: the hot
path compares it with `==` against the request
method, so an operand carrying a space or another
non-token character can never match and is
rejected at config load.

Istio StringMatch shape — EXACTLY one of
`exact` / `prefix` / `regex`. The runtime is an
externally tagged enum, so both `{}` and
`{"exact": "GET", "prefix": "G"}` are rejected.
Prefix patterns are uppercased at compile time
(methods are uppercase ASCII per RFC 9110 §9.1);
regex patterns are interpreted verbatim inside
full-input anchors. `exact` / `prefix` operands
must be non-empty method tokens (case and
extension methods such as `PROPFIND` are
preserved); `regex` is a pattern rather than a
token and is only checked for regex validity.

methods.description: HTTP methods (any-of). Empty = no method restriction.

propertyNames.description:
Header names are RFC 9110 tokens, normalized to ASCII
lowercase at config load. A name outside the token
grammar (empty, `x bad`, `x:bad`) can never appear in
a parsed request header map, so it is rejected at
config load rather than admitted as a rule that
silently never fires.

oneOf.description: Bare-string back-compat form, interpreted as Exact.

Istio StringMatch shape — EXACTLY one of
`exact` / `prefix` / `regex`. The runtime is an
externally tagged enum, so both `{}` and
`{"exact": "a", "prefix": "b"}` are rejected.
An empty `exact` is a legitimate "header present
and empty" predicate; empty `prefix` / `regex`
operands are rejected at config load.

headers.description: Header matches (all-of). Header names are case-insensitive.

without_headers.description:
Negated header matches (Istio `withoutHeaders`), keyed
and normalized exactly like `headers`. The rule fails
when ANY listed header is present and its value
satisfies the matcher; an absent header never vetoes
the rule, so `{"x-legacy": {"regex": ".*"}}` requires
the header to be absent.

port.description:
Destination port the client addressed (Istio
`HTTPMatchRequest.port`), read from trusted provenance
only: the original destination when capture rewrote the
accept socket, otherwise the frontend listener port —
never `Host` or forwarding headers. A request with
neither does not match.

oneOf.description:
Istio StringMatch shape — EXACTLY one of `exact` /
`prefix` / `regex`. `regex` must match the full
decoded value; empty `prefix` / `regex` operands
are rejected at config load.

query_params.description: Query parameter matches (all-of), compared after percent-decoding the backend-bound query representation available at the dispatch hook, including authentication-owned credential strips and any priority-overridden request_transformer that already ran. A deliberately later route/request transform remains a separate ordered operation. A request whose query cannot be decoded to one value is rejected with 400 before any rule is evaluated: a repeated or percent-encoded duplicate name, a literal '+' (RFC 3986 plus vs form-urlencoded space), an unencoded ';' (a pair separator for backends that also split on ';'; '%3B' is unambiguous), malformed percent-encoding, or a non-UTF-8 decoding.

uri.description:
Optional URI predicate (Istio `StringMatch` shape).
Exactly one of `exact` / `prefix` / `regex`. This is
normally omitted because the parent proxy `listen_path`
gates URI selection; the VirtualService translator emits
it for widened `ignoreUriCase` routes and collapsed
route-order fallbacks that need dispatch-layer URI
precision. Regex patterns must match the full URI path.

ignore_uri_case.description:
When true, folds ASCII case for `match.uri.exact` and
`match.uri.prefix` comparisons only. Regex URI matches
keep their operator-supplied regex unchanged; operators
who want case-insensitive regex should write `(?i)` in
the pattern. Requires `match.uri`.

source_namespace.description:
Source workload Kubernetes namespace (exact match).
Mirrors Istio `VirtualService.http[].match.sourceNamespace`:
the CRD models this as an exact-only string (no
`prefix`/`regex` arms). Resolved from the peer's SPIFFE
ID via the Istio convention
`spiffe://<trust-domain>/ns/<namespace>/sa/<service-account>`.
Matches are case-sensitive (Kubernetes namespace names
are RFC 1123 lowercase). The predicate fails closed
(returns no-match) when the request carries no resolved
peer SPIFFE identity, so non-mesh requests and clients
that present non-SPIFFE certificates do not match.
Empty / whitespace-only values are rejected at load time.

authority.description:
`:authority` / `Host` match (Istio `HTTPMatchRequest.authority`).
Exactly one of `exact` / `prefix` / `regex` per rule.
Exact and prefix patterns compare against the raw request
`Host`/`:authority` case-sensitively, including an
explicit request port when present. Regex patterns are
compiled verbatim and must match the full authority
string; operators who want case-insensitive regex should
write `(?i)` in the pattern. Distinct from
VirtualService-level `hosts`, which gates proxy
admission — this is a per-rule predicate evaluated AFTER
routing has picked the proxy.

oneOf.description: Bare-string back-compat form, interpreted as Exact.

destination.description:
Override applied on match. At least one field must be set
(enforced at rule level, where a `redirect` rule is allowed
to omit `destination` entirely). `upstream_id` is mutually
exclusive with the direct-backend fields
(`backend_host`/`backend_port`/`backend_tls`);
`backend_host` and `backend_port` must be set together, and
`backend_tls` requires both.

backend_host.description:
Direct-backend host. This is a BARE host — a DNS name,
an IPv4 literal, or an IPv6 literal in either `::1` or
`[::1]` form — with the port carried by `backend_port`.
The dispatch path hands the value straight to DNS
resolution, so an embedded authority port, scheme, path,
query, fragment, or userinfo resolves to nothing and is
rejected at config load rather than answering 502 on
every matching request. Leading / trailing whitespace is
trimmed and the value is ASCII-lowercased at load, so
the length bound applies to the TRIMMED value at
runtime while `maxLength` here counts the raw string.
The pattern is likewise a conservative approximation:
the runtime additionally parses the IPv6 forms, so a
colon-bearing value that is not a valid IPv6 literal
(`1:2:3`) passes this schema and is still refused at
admission.

backend_tls.description: Optional per-rule backend TLS override (direct backends only).

requires_node_waypoint_authz.description:
Trusted mesh-translator marker. When scoped NodeWaypoint
authorization is active, a matching destination carrying
this marker requires an authorized destination stamp.

timeout_ms.description:
Optional route-local backend response/read timeout in
milliseconds. Mutually exclusive with
`timeout_disabled: true`. `0` means "no timeout" and is the
value `timeout_disabled: true` resolves to.

timeout_disabled.description:
Explicitly clear the selected proxy's inherited backend
response/read timeout. Cannot be true when `timeout_ms` is set.

request_timeout_ms.description:
Optional TOTAL request deadline for this rule, in
milliseconds from request receipt (Gateway API
`HTTPRoute.rules[].timeouts.request`). Unlike `timeout_ms`,
which bounds one backend attempt's wait for response headers
and the idle gap between response frames, it spans every
attempt, retry backoff, and the streaming response body, and
is never re-armed by a retry. Request-scoped: it never changes
the selected proxy or upstream. Expiry before a non-gRPC
response head answers `504` (with `X-Gateway-Error:
request_timeout` when no backend held the request, otherwise
`backend_timeout`); expiry mid-body resets the HTTP/2
stream, closes the HTTP/1.1 connection, or resets the
HTTP/3 stream with `H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED`; a gRPC request
folds it into its RPC deadline and ends with
`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and native HTTP/3
enforce it alike. Expiry is charged to a backend's health
only when that backend held the cancelled attempt; expiry
before the attempt was handed to a backend, in retry backoff,
or after the response head is health-neutral. Upgraded
WebSocket / CONNECT-UDP tunnels are not bounded by it. `0` is
rejected; omit the field for no route deadline.

attempt_timeout_ms.description:
Optional TOTAL bound on each backend attempt for this rule, in
milliseconds (Gateway API
`HTTPRoute.rules[].timeouts.backendRequest`, which the
translator also projects as `timeout_ms`). The budget starts
when the attempt is handed to the backend and covers its
response head and its whole response body; every retry
attempt gets a fresh budget, and `request_timeout_ms`, when
set, still bounds the whole transaction. It is independent of
`timeout_ms` / `timeout_disabled`, which keep bounding the
header wait and the idle gap between frames. Expiry before a
non-gRPC response head answers the ordinary backend-timeout
`504` (retried when the rule's `retry` lists `504`); expiry
after the head has been sent is never retried and cuts the
body exactly like `request_timeout_ms` does (HTTP/2 stream
reset, HTTP/1.1 connection close, HTTP/3
`H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED` stream reset, health-neutral). A gRPC
request folds it into its RPC deadline, anchored when the rule
is selected and re-armed for each retry attempt, and ends with
`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and native HTTP/3
enforce it alike. Request-scoped: it never changes the
selected proxy or upstream. `0` is rejected; omit the field
for no per-attempt total bound.

retry.description:
Optional route-local retry policy. Mutually exclusive with
`retry_disabled: true`. Request-scoped: it replaces the
selected proxy's retry policy only for requests this rule
matches. Istio `VirtualService.http[].retries` and Gateway
API `HTTPRoute.rules[].retry` are projected here; the Gateway
API translator emits `max_retries` = `attempts` (retries
after the initial attempt), `retryable_status_codes` =
`codes`, a `fixed` backoff of `backoff`, the default
replay-safe `retryable_methods`, and
`retry_on_connect_failure: true`. Backoff and every attempt
stay inside the rule's `request_timeout_ms` budget.

retry_disabled.description:
Explicitly clear the selected proxy's inherited retry
policy. Cannot be true when `retry` is set.

request_transform.description:
Per-rule request header transforms (Istio VirtualService
`http[].headers.request.{set,add,remove}`). Published onto
`RequestContext.route_override_request_transform` when this
rule matches. Every enabled `request_transformer` on the
proxy applies only its static header rules first; proxy core
then applies this list exactly once after the last eligible
(enabled) instance so route-level header writes win under
multiple same-type instances and priority overrides. A
disabled RTDS transformer is not eligible and does not
consume the list. `apply_route_overrides: true` lets an
auto-emitted empty-rules instance act as that eligible
consumer. Validated at config load — CRLF in values,
unknown operations, and `add`/`update` destinations in the
gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace or
the router's `x-path-param-*` route-capture namespace
(case-insensitive, `_` or `-`) are rejected. The request list
is applied after the LATER of the last eligible consumer and
the last dispatch instance, so a consumer a priority override
moves ahead of the dispatcher still applies it. An effective
chain whose rules carry `request_transform` but that has no
configured `request_transformer` is refused at plugin-cache
construction and admin admission (the list would otherwise be
silently dropped); an RTDS-disabled transformer still counts
as configured.

value.description: Required and non-null for add/update; omitted or null for remove.

response_transform.description:
Per-rule response header transforms (Istio VirtualService
`http[].headers.response.{set,add,remove}`). Same shape as
`request_transform` but applied on the response path: every
enabled `response_transformer` applies static header rules
first, then proxy core applies this list exactly once after
the last eligible instance (ordinary H1/H2/H3, synthetic/
rejection, header simulation, and deadline provenance paths).

Because this publishes onto the `response_transformer`
write surface, it shares that plugin's closed destination
set: add/update of a protocol-managed hop-by-hop or
framing name (`connection`, `content-length`,
`keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`,
`te`, `trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`,
case-insensitive) is rejected at construction. Remove of
those names remains allowed. `request_transform` keeps its
existing contract. An effective chain whose rules carry
`response_transform` but that has no configured
`response_transformer` is refused at plugin-cache
construction and admin admission.

value.description: Required and non-null for add/update; omitted or null for remove.

fault.description:
Optional per-rule fault action; `null` is accepted and means
"no fault", exactly as omitting the key does. Projects Istio
`VirtualService.http[].fault` onto the matched dispatch
rule (replacing the historical proxy-scoped
`fault_injection` plugin that could not be collapsed
with sibling routes). At least one of `delay` / `abort`
must be present.

RTDS scope: the percentages baked into a per-rule fault
are NOT runtime-tunable via the GAP-3E RTDS keys
`ferrum.fault_injection.<scope>.{abort,delay}_percent` —
those keys apply only to `fault_injection` plugin
instances configured with `runtime_overlay_scope`.
Operators who need RTDS-driven fault percentages
should use a global / proxy-scoped `fault_injection`
plugin instead.

duration_ms.description:
Sleep duration in milliseconds before dispatch
when the percentile roll hits. Bounded to
`[1, 60_000]` (1 ms to 1 minute).

percentage.description:
Percent of matching requests that trigger the
delay. `0.0` is rejected at config load time
(omit the action to disable it instead). Positive
values below one 64-bit sampler bucket round up
to that first bucket so every accepted value can
trigger.

Percent of matching requests that abort. Positive
values below one 64-bit sampler bucket round up to
that first bucket so every accepted value can trigger.

grpc_status.description:
Optional gRPC status code emitted only when the
immutable pre-plugin request flavor is native
gRPC. Plain HTTP, WebSocket, and gRPC-Web requests
never receive a stray `grpc-status` header even if
an earlier hook rewrites `content-type`.

body.description: Optional response body; empty when omitted.

rewrite.description:
Optional per-rule URI / authority rewrite; `null` is
accepted and means "no rewrite". Projects Istio
`VirtualService.http[].rewrite` onto the matched dispatch
rule so a rewriting route can be collapsed with sibling
routes onto one Ferrum proxy without rewriting the siblings'
traffic. At least one of `uri` / `authority` must be set.
Applied when the rule matches and no `redirect` fires.

uri.description:
Replacement request path forwarded to the backend. When
`match_prefix` is set (the source `match.uri` was a
prefix) only that prefix is replaced; otherwise the whole
path is replaced. Must be a canonical absolute path
without a query or fragment. Percent escapes, dot
segments, backslashes, and CRLF are rejected at load
time (the schema only checks the leading `/`; full
canonical-path admission is a runtime check). The
composed path is checked again before policy and
dispatch; ambiguous paths are refused, not resolved.

authority.description:
Replacement `Host` / `:authority` forwarded to the
backend. Must be exactly `host` or `host:port`: a DNS
name or IPv4 literal (letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `_`) or a
bracketed IPv6 literal, optionally followed by a decimal
port 1-65535. A path, query, fragment, userinfo,
whitespace, or bare IPv6 literal is rejected at load. The
runtime additionally parses the IPv6 literal and the port
range, which the pattern only approximates.

match_prefix.description:
Literal path prefix the source `match.uri.prefix`
matched. The plugin replaces exactly this prefix with
`uri` and appends the unmatched suffix VERBATIM (Istio
`HTTPRewrite` / Envoy `prefix_rewrite`), so a prefix
ending inside a path segment keeps that segment: with
`match_prefix: /prefix/old` and `uri: /new`,
`/prefix/oldtail` forwards as `/newtail`. A separator is
never synthesized; a doubled one is collapsed when both
sides carry a `/`. An empty string strips nothing and
prepends `uri` (the Gateway API root `PathPrefix: /`
case); omit the field for whole-path replacement. A
`match_prefix` with no `uri` is inert and dropped.
Normally set by the VirtualService or Gateway API
translator, not hand-authored.

redirect.description:
Optional per-rule HTTP redirect; `null` is accepted and
means "no redirect" (a rule that is `null` here still needs
a `destination`). Projects Istio
`VirtualService.http[].redirect`. When the rule matches the
request is answered with a 3xx + `Location` and never reaches
a backend; takes precedence over `rewrite` and the route
override destination. A status-only redirect is valid and
preserves the original URL. A rule carrying a `redirect`
does not require a `destination`. `port` and `derive_port`
are mutually exclusive (Istio oneof); scheme-default ports
are omitted from Location.

uri.description:
Replacement path for the Location header; request path
preserved when unset. Must be an absolute path (leading
`/`) of printable ASCII only — no fragment, whitespace,
raw control byte, or unencoded non-ASCII, query included
— whose path
component is already canonical (dot segments,
backslashes, and escapes that decode differently are
rejected at load — a runtime check the pattern does not
express). It may carry its own `?query` unless
`match_prefix` is set, because the unmatched request
suffix is appended after `uri`.

match_prefix.description:
Literal matched path prefix replaced by `uri`; the
unmatched suffix is appended verbatim, exactly as for
`rewrite.match_prefix` (no separator is synthesized at a
boundary that had none). An empty string strips nothing
and prepends `uri`; omit the field for whole-path
replacement. Normally emitted by the VirtualService or
Gateway API translator.

authority.description:
Replacement authority (`host` or `host:port`) for the
Location header; request authority preserved when unset.
Same grammar as `rewrite.authority`.

port.description:
Replacement authority port (Istio `redirect.port`); request
host is preserved when authority is unset. Mutually
exclusive with `derive_port`. Scheme-default ports
(`80`/`http`, `443`/`https`) are omitted from Location.

derive_port.description:
Dynamically derive the Location authority port (Istio
`redirect.derivePort`). `FROM_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT` uses 80 for
http and 443 for https (including when `scheme` is set on
the same redirect). `FROM_REQUEST_PORT` uses the trusted
request port: original-destination port when capture
rewrote the accept socket, otherwise the frontend listener
port — never spoofable `X-Forwarded-Port` / `Forwarded`
headers. Mutually exclusive with `port`.

scheme.description:
Replacement scheme for the Location header; request
scheme preserved when unset. The constructor
ASCII-lowercases the value before checking it, so
`HTTPS` and `Https` are accepted and stored as `https`.

redirect_code.description: HTTP redirect status code (Istio `redirectCode`). Defaults to 301.

reject_unmatched.description:
When `true`, requests that match no rule are rejected with 404
instead of falling through to the proxy's default backend. The
Istio VirtualService translator sets this so a route gated by a
method/header/query-param `match` does not serve traffic that
misses those predicates. Across multiple attached instances, the
decision is finalized only after all instances run and only when
no instance matched and no earlier route override exists.

weighted_splits.description:
Weighted splits dispatched leg by leg (issue #7387). When the
destination the whole dispatch group selects is one of these
`upstream_id`s (a matched rule's `destination.upstream_id`, or the
route's own `upstream_id` when no rule overrides it), the dispatch
finalizer the plugin cache installs after the last instance picks
one leg by weight (an exact, interleaved weighted cycle) and sends
the request through that leg's own upstream, so the leg's own
DestinationRule projection and authorization apply to exactly the
requests it receives. A split no leg was selected for is never
dispatched. NodeWaypoint mesh slice preparation writes this for a
VirtualService split that names a DestinationRule-governed Service
or external host and refuses a carried route that already carries
it.

upstream_id.description: The split destination this entry resolves; unique per instance.

The upstream this leg dispatches through. Distinct
within the split and never itself a weighted split.

weight.description: The leg's share, relative to the other legs.

originate_tls.description:
Dial this leg over TLS (backend scheme `https`) with
its upstream's backend TLS settings. The selected leg
decides the request's backend scheme; a leg without
it keeps the route's own scheme. NodeWaypoint slice
preparation sets it on an external host's leg whose
DestinationRule `tls.mode` originates TLS (`SIMPLE`,
`MUTUAL`, `ISTIO_MUTUAL`) on that port, never on a
Service leg, which keeps the mesh transport.

MeshRouteRetryConfig.description:
Strict route-local retry policy for mesh_route_dispatch. Unknown keys
(for example `max_retry` or `retry_on_connect_failur`) fail admission
instead of silently falling back to defaults. The numeric bounds below
mirror the shared gateway `RetryConfig` field validation the route
policy runs after deserialization.

items.description:
One of GET / POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE / HEAD / OPTIONS /
TRACE / CONNECT. The validator ASCII-uppercases before
comparing, so `get` and `Get` are accepted.
